title: Motivation: Hunger, Thirst, Sex
summary: Biological motives: hunger, thirst and sexual response, homeostatic regulation by the hypothalamus, and set-point theory.
objectives: Describe hypothalamic regulation of hunger and thirst.
revision: Biological motives: hunger, thirst, sexual motivation; hypothalamic regulation; set-point theory and homeostasis.
traps: Homeostasis: stable internal environment via negative feedback.
Set point: genetically influenced weight range maintained by hunger/satiety.

notes.t: The physiological drive to eat, regulated by the hypothalamus (lateral hypothalamus = hunger centre; ventromedial hypothalamus = satiety centre).
Set-point theory: the body maintains a genetically influenced weight range; hunger signals when energy stores fall below the set point.
Thirst is triggered by decreased blood volume/increased osmolality, detected by hypothalamic osmoreceptors, producing drinking behaviour.
Sexual response is regulated by the hypothalamus and hormones (testosterone, oestrogen), but unlike hunger/thirst is not essential for individual survival.
The maintenance of a stable internal environment through negative-feedback regulation.
UGC NET frequently asks about hypothalamic regulation of hunger/thirst/sex and homeostasis/set-point theory.
